issues.title: Restore 'create Derivative Works from' to the confidential-information use restriction
issues.planned_action: Re-insert the deleted phrase so Provider is barred from creating derivative works from LargeCo confidential information, matching the walk-away no-derivative-works restriction.

issues.title: Add confidentiality/data-security/no-training carve-out to the liability cap
issues.planned_action: Insert a carve-out from the standard 12-month-fees cap for breach of confidentiality, data security, or the no-training restriction, in exchange for accepting AgentCo's refusal to broaden Section 8 indemnification beyond third-party IP claims.

issues.title: Reinstate a narrowed security audit right (SOC 2 + reasonable information requests)
issues.planned_action: Replace the wholesale-deleted Security Audit Rights clause with a narrower right requiring an annual SOC 2 (or equivalent) report plus reasonable additional security information on request, using AgentCo's own SOC 2 offer (cmt-1076) rather than the on-site/penetration-test audit model AgentCo rejected.

issues.title: Tighten breach notification timing and restore suspected-breach trigger
issues.planned_action: Move the hard notification cap from AgentCo's countered 48 hours back to 24 hours, and restore 'suspected' breaches and third-party claims/threats as notice triggers, while keeping AgentCo's 'reasonable efforts' wording and 24-hour soft target.

issues.title: Narrow the AI-specific representations instead of deleting them wholesale
issues.planned_action: Reinsert the AI rep/warranty clause without the absolute 'will render accurate and reliable results' claim (consistent with TalentFlow's decision-support positioning), keeping the industry-standard development/security/monitoring warranty and the training-data-rights/transparency warranty.

issues.title: Require consent before AgentCo uses LargeCo's name or logo
issues.planned_action: Add a written-consent requirement to the reference/logo-use clause, picking up AgentCo's own openness to a limitation (cmt-465).

issues.title: Restore media-company insurance rider and no-cost risk-transfer endorsements
issues.planned_action: Accept AgentCo's reduced per-occurrence/aggregate dollar limits as reasonable for a Series A vendor at pilot scale, but restore the media-company coverage rider, the Commercial Crime loss-payee endorsement, and the Additional Insured / Waiver of Subrogation / primary-non-contributory endorsements, none of which carry a marginal cost tied to policy limits.

issues.title: Fix undefined 'Transition Period' reference in the data-export/disposal clause
issues.planned_action: Remove the undefined 'Transition Period' term flagged by AgentCo (cmt-411) while preserving the 60-day post-termination export window.

issues.title: Fix garbled 'ustomer' merge artifact in the Documentation definition
issues.planned_action: Correct the corrupted defined term so the Documentation definition reads 'available to Customer' rather than 'available to ustomer'.

dispositions.reason: Party-name conversion (AgentCo/Customer) is mechanical and already mutually confirmed (cmt-0, cmt-10).

AgentCo's rejection of the standalone 'Deliverables' definition and ownership clause (cmt-71), and the definition renumbering that followed it, are acceptable because Section 4.1 already gives Customer ownership of all Content, defined to include Output -- the candidate summaries and interview notes TalentFlow generates. That existing clause independently satisfies LargeCo's requirement that AI-generated work product remain LargeCo-owned, making the duplicate Deliverables clause unnecessary. The Term-scoped, non-exclusive access license at p-024 also gives LargeCo everything it needs for a pilot that ends with the Term.

Customer Data ownership, payment terms, cure periods, and the post-termination data export/deletion terms (cmt-120, cmt-130, cmt-145) are already resolved and consistent with LargeCo's data-return requirements.

AgentCo's refusal to broaden Section 8 indemnification beyond third-party IP claims (cmt-170) is a realistic limit for a Series A vendor and is accepted, and the conform-to-specifications disclaimer is fine given TalentFlow's decision-support framing. But confidentiality, data-security, and no-training breaches still need a stronger remedy than the standard fees-paid cap -- addressed via a liability-cap carve-out at p-074 (T-02) rather than expanded indemnification.

The bulk of the AI/service representations list (a)-(l) was adopted; AgentCo's rejection of sub-clause (j) (no recurring customer complaints) is operational-quality boilerplate that doesn't touch data security, confidentiality, training, or ownership. But AgentCo deleted the entire separate AI-specific representations clause (cmt-334), objecting mainly to the 'accurate and reliable results' warranty given user-controlled inputs -- fair, and in tension with TalentFlow's own decision-support framing. The clause's training-data-rights warranty is a separate, important commitment that shouldn't have been deleted along with it. See T-05.
General-terms heading, severability, and open-source warranty are standard and unchanged in substance.

Mutual assignment rights are already agreed (cmt-384). Subcontracting is fine as a general responsibility clause because the DPA's Sub-Processor engagement/objection mechanism (Section 3.8) already gives LargeCo notice and objection rights specific to Customer Data, which is where the real risk sits (cmt-389).
AgentCo accepted nearly all of the restrictive confidential-information use language but deleted 'create Derivative Works from.' That's a walk-away gap -- addressed in T-01.

The 60-day post-termination export/support right is sound, but it references an undefined 'Transition Period' that AgentCo correctly flagged (cmt-411); we confirmed the fix by reply and standalone comment since the underlying text isn't independently addressable in this draft. AgentCo's added 'at Customer's expense' qualifier for export support is a reasonable cost allocation. The clause-grouping point in cmt-408 is organizational only -- the disposal and injunctive-relief rights stand regardless of how they're grouped.

AgentCo narrowed the injunctive-relief trigger to confidentiality-obligation breaches specifically, which is precise rather than a weakening -- confidentiality is exactly the category where LargeCo needs the equitable remedy.

Usage Data is defined to exclude Customer Data and Content, so using it to improve the platform doesn't touch candidate data (cmt-459). The No Training clause remains intact with only a narrow, necessary cloud-storage carve-out (AWS) for retention, not for training or human review (cmt-460) -- this satisfies the no-training requirement cleanly.
AgentCo signaled openness to limiting the name/logo-use right (cmt-465); addressed in T-06.
The shift from arbitration to Delaware governing law was already mutually accepted (cmt-470) in an earlier turn; not revisiting a closed, non-core point.
Notice, no-waiver, and entire-agreement clauses are standard and unchanged in substance.

AgentCo declined to narrow the mutual export-control compliance list (cmt-484, reply to cmt-483). The broader list doesn't create asymmetric risk for LargeCo, which must comply with export control law regardless; not worth re-litigating.
Force majeure carve-outs and the Feedback IP-ownership clause (Customer retains Feedback IP, grants back a limited license, no attribution) already match LargeCo's required position (cmt-489).

DPA scope, roles, definitions, Customer Instructions, and notice-to-Customer obligations are AgentCo's own template terms and already satisfy LargeCo's subprocessor-transparency and data-flow requirements.

The imported Information Security Program requirements (encryption, access controls, segregation, authentication) were substantially adopted; AgentCo's removal of a customer-review right over its Information Security Program summary (p-175) is a minor scope trim that doesn't undercut the underlying security commitments. We used AgentCo's own DPA audit clause (Section 3.7, p-152) to formalize the SOC 2 offer from cmt-1076 -- see T-03.

Equipment pre-approval, source-code hardening/testing rights, and LargeCo's unilateral code-analysis right are exactly the category of controls that belong with privileged system access or future integrations, not this SaaS-access pilot where AgentCo has no access to LargeCo systems or facilities (cmt-805). The wholesale-deleted Security Audit Rights clause at p-183 is addressed separately below (counter) since AgentCo volunteered a SOC 2 alternative worth capturing in the Agreement.

AgentCo rejected the entire Security Audit Rights clause outright rather than just the invasive elements, but also volunteered a SOC 2 report as an alternative (cmt-1076). That offer should be captured in the Agreement rather than left as an uncommitted comment -- see T-03 (implemented at p-152).

Extending the security-flaw response commitment from 8 to 24 hours (p-180) is a reasonable accommodation for a smaller vendor and is distinct from Data Security Breach notification timing, addressed separately below. Breach investigation cooperation, credit monitoring (now made subject to the liability cap per AgentCo's edit), third-party beneficiary rights, the security manager designation, and the tracking-technology restrictions are all substantially adopted.

AgentCo doubled the breach-notification soft target (8 to 24 hours) and hard cap (24 to 48 hours) and dropped 'suspected' breaches and third-party claims/threats as triggers, with no stated rationale. We moved a tightened 24-hour, suspected-breach-inclusive notification duty into DPA Section 3.2 (p-142) since this section isn't independently addressable in the current draft -- see T-04.
Background-check requirements belong with privileged system/facility access, which AgentCo doesn't have for this SaaS-access pilot (cmt-1427).
Schedule 1 processing details and the SLA/Support Policy exhibit heading are AgentCo's own template terms; substance is addressed in the next range.

AgentCo declined to adopt a bespoke enterprise SLA and instead offered its standard published support policy (cmt-1582). For a six-month, 150-user pilot this is proportionate -- the standard 99.9% uptime target and published severity/response framework are adequate for an evaluation deployment, and none of LargeCo's walk-away data-security or governance requirements depend on the SLA exhibit.
No substantive content in this stretch of the SLA exhibit.
Reduced per-occurrence/aggregate insurance limits ($2M rather than $5M) for Commercial General Liability and Workers' Compensation are proportionate for a Series A SaaS vendor at pilot scale.

Marking Contractors Pollution Liability as Not Applicable (p-383) is reasonable since AgentCo does no physical/environmental work. But the media-company coverage rider, the Commercial Crime loss-payee endorsement, and the Additional Insured/Waiver of Subrogation endorsements were deleted without any stated rationale and carry no marginal premium tied to policy limits -- addressed in T-07.
The Documentation definition substantively matches what LargeCo needs, but a merge artifact corrupted 'Customer' into 'ustomer' -- fixed in T-09.

AgentCo's comment about clause grouping (disposal, injunctive relief) is an organizational preference; the underlying substantive rights (60-day export window, injunctive relief for confidentiality breach) are preserved regardless of how they're grouped, so no edit is needed.
